Ezra Klein's sweeping interview with Bernie Sanders

Bernie is the man! He's got some great ideas and some great arguments to support his stance. All around, he would be a very solid candidate if he gets the nomination. I wonder, though, how he plans to sell his ideas to unaffiliated voters in a highly polarized general election.

My sense is that he will expand his messaging and language as he realizes what people respond to, while maintaining the same underlying principles.

But my biggest belief on that issues is that the only way for unaffiliated voters to be convinced is for people like you and me to talk to everyone we know about Bernie Sanders!

A fantastic interview that covers a wide range of topics. Some of my favorite quotes that concisely capture his attitude and candor...

On equality, a big theme in Bernie's campaign:

It seems to me that when you look at basic necessities of life — education, health care, nutrition — there must be a guarantee that people receive what they need in order to live a dignified life.

On foreign policy and war:

When you talk about foreign policy you're talking about many, many things, but maybe the most important thing that you're talking about is war.

On Israel and Palestine:

A Zionist? What does that mean? Want to define what the word is? Do I think Israel has the right to exist, yeah, I do. Do I believe that the United States should be playing an even-handed role in terms of its dealings with the Palestinian community in Israel? Absolutely I do.

On climate change:

I happen to believe that when you talk about foreign policy, a the very top of the list is the need for the United States to lead the world, to work with China, work with Russia, work with India in transforming our energy system away from fossil fuels and into energy efficiency and sustainable energy. This is not just an "environmental issue," this is also a global national security issue as well.

On foreign trade policy with China:

As I indicated to you earlier, I am an internationalist. I want to see poor people around the world see their standard of living increase, but you talk about zero sum. A lot of people tell me the American worker's going to have to become poorer so we can help poor people in China. I don't believe that for a second. I want to see the people in China live in a democratic society with a higher standard of living. I want to see that, but I don't think that has to take place at the expense of the American worker. I don't think decent-paying jobs in this country have got to be lost as companies shut down here and move to China. I want to see the Chinese people do as well, but I do not want to see the collapse of the American middle class take place, and I will fight against that as hard as I can.
